guarantees.claim: txcnt_eq_blksz is 0 when digest_size_i is not SHA2_256, SHA2_384, or SHA2_512 (including the default case)
When digest_size_i equals SHA2_256, txcnt_eq_blksz is assigned (txcount[BlockSizeBitsSHA256-1:0] == 0) && (txcount != 0)
When digest_size_i equals SHA2_384 or SHA2_512, txcnt_eq_blksz is assigned (txcount[BlockSizeBitsSHA512-1:0] == 0) && (txcount != 0)

assumptions.claim: digest_size_i is restricted to SHA2_256, SHA2_384, or SHA2_512; any other value keeps txcnt_eq_blksz permanently 0
assumptions.cond: when HMAC block-boundary logic relies on txcnt_eq_blksz
assumptions.risk: txcnt_eq_blksz never asserts, breaking block processing and potentially causing incorrect HMAC output

assumptions.claim: txcount bit width is at least BlockSizeBitsSHA512 bits (or at least BlockSizeBitsSHA256 if SHA2_256 is the only mode selected)
assumptions.cond: when using SHA2_384 or SHA2_512 mode
assumptions.risk: bit slice txcount[BlockSizeBitsSHA512-1:0] is out of bounds, leading to undefined synthesis behavior or false block-size matches

uncertain_points.claim: If digest_size_i can be set to SHA2_512 while txcount bit width is less than BlockSizeBitsSHA512, the bit selection txcount[BlockSizeBitsSHA512-1:0] is illegal
uncertain_points.cond: legal configuration allows SHA2_512 mode with a narrow txcount counter
uncertain_points.risk: synthesis may issue error or produce a truncated compare, yielding spurious block-boundary assertions

uncertain_points.claim: txcnt_eq_blksz is 0 when txcount == 0, even in a valid mode; it is unclear if a zero-length message should ever trigger a block-boundary flag
uncertain_points.cond: txcount == 0 and digest_size_i in {SHA2_256, SHA2_384, SHA2_512}
uncertain_points.risk: if HMAC expects a block-boundary flag at start of message, this may delay or skip padding
